questions.question: On which date did the Constituent Assembly of India adopt the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted India's Constitution on 26 November 1949; most provisions came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution protects life and personal liberty?
questions.explanation: Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part IV, Articles 36 to 51, contains the Directive Principles of State Policy; Part III contains Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule for rural Panchayati Raj institutions.

questions.question: Who ordinarily presides over a sitting of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Speaker presides over Lok Sabha sittings, maintains order and applies the House's rules of procedure.

questions.question: Which court can directly be approached under Article 32 for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of the Fundamental Rights in Part III.

questions.question: Which Veda is generally regarded as the oldest of the four Vedas?
questions.explanation: The Rigveda is the earliest of the four Vedic collections and principally contains hymns to Vedic deities.

questions.question: In which city did the uprising of 1857 begin among sepoys on 10 May 1857?
questions.explanation: The sepoy uprising broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857 before rebels proceeded towards Delhi.

questions.question: The Dandi March of 1930 protested which colonial measure?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's march from Sabarmati to Dandi challenged the British salt monopoly and the tax on salt.

questions.question: The Chauri Chaura incident of 1922 is linked to the withdrawal of which movement?
questions.explanation: Following the violence at Chauri Chaura in February 1922, Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.question: The 'Arthashastra' is traditionally attributed to which scholar?
questions.explanation: The treatise on statecraft and economic administration is traditionally associated with Kautilya, also called Chanakya.

questions.question: Which Indian state contains the famous Sun Temple at Konark?
questions.explanation: The thirteenth-century Konark Sun Temple stands on the Odisha coast and is dedicated to Surya.

questions.question: Which physical feature runs broadly parallel to the western coast of peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats form a mountain chain along the western side of peninsular India, broadly parallel to the Arabian Sea coast.

questions.question: The Godavari is often called the Dakshin Ganga. Into which water body does it empty?
questions.explanation: The Godavari flows generally east across peninsular India and forms a delta along the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Black or regur soil of the Deccan is particularly well suited to which major crop?
questions.explanation: Black cotton soil retains moisture and is traditionally associated with cotton cultivation in much of the Deccan plateau.

questions.question: Chilika Lake, a large brackish-water lagoon, lies in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Chilika is a brackish-water lagoon situated on the Odisha coast, separated from the Bay of Bengal by a sandy barrier.

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park, associated with the Indian one-horned rhinoceros, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga is in Assam and is internationally known for its conservation of the greater one-horned rhinoceros.

questions.question: Most of Earth's protective atmospheric ozone layer occurs in which layer?
questions.explanation: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, where it absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.question: Which element is present at the centre of the haem group in haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron in the haem group of haemoglobin binds oxygen reversibly and helps transport it through blood.

questions.question: A prolonged deficiency of vitamin C causes which condition?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is required for normal collagen formation; severe deficiency causes scurvy with bleeding gums and impaired wound healing.

questions.question: Which plant tissue chiefly conducts water and dissolved minerals from roots towards leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and mineral ions upward through vessels and tracheids; phloem chiefly transports sugars.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms (Ω); by Ohm's law, one ohm equals one volt per ampere.

questions.question: Which device is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, while a hygrometer measures humidity and an anemometer measures wind speed.

questions.question: In which year did the Reserve Bank of India begin operations?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India commenced operations on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a direct tax in India?
questions.explanation: Income tax is levied directly on the income of persons or entities; GST, customs duty and excise duty are indirect taxes.
